title: Pompeii Wardrobe Opens After Almost 2,000 Years
paragraphs: Archaeologists in Pompeii have opened a wooden cupboard that stayed closed for almost 2,000 years. The Archaeological Park of Pompeii announced the find in late October 2026. The cupboard was in a house on the Via dell'Abbondanza, one of the busiest streets of the ancient Roman city, which was buried by the eruption of Mount Vesuvius in the year 79.

The objects inside were simple but personal. They included a necklace with at least 24 small amulets, 38 bronze coins, tweezers, a small glass bottle for perfume or oil, an incense burner and several pots and vessels. A wooden box with lead weights suggests that someone in the household worked in trade. Archaeologists also found mouse bones in a storage jar, which shows that even ancient homes had pest problems.

Because the coins and the necklace were left behind, researchers think the owners may have escaped in a hurry. However, this is only an interpretation. The site director, Gabriel Zuchtriegel, said that it is impossible to know with certainty who lived in the house, and nobody can say whether the family survived the eruption.

questions.a: That someone in the household worked in trade.

questions.q: What is uncertain about the owners?
questions.a: Who they were and whether they survived the eruption.
